messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep on the 8xA100 rack (mixed NVLink/PCIe) with TP=2 PP=2 and noticed a ~30% throughput regression when TP shards crossed an NVLink boundary. sharing snippets below.

maya: repro command I used:
```
./run_inference_profile.sh --model redwood-7b --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch 64 --seq 1024 --fabric mv2:nvlink:2,pci:6 --profile=offload
```

jon: can you paste the numbers? p50/p99 or tokens/sec?

maya: numbers from the same job id 2026-03-10-007:
```
tokens/sec: baseline(localized shards on same NVLink domain) = 4200
tokens/sec: crossed-NVLink = 2900
all_reduce mean: baseline 12.3ms -> crossed 37.1ms
kv_cache_prefetch PCIe copy: 4.6ms -> 13.2ms
```

alejandra: hmm that all_reduce blow-up smells like extra serialization on the fallback kernel path. did you capture the kernel selection log?

maya: yep — relevant excerpt from runtime.kernelselect logs:
```
[2026-03-10T15:02:01Z] shard0 -> selected kernel: fused_attention_gtx_x8_qkv_fast (nvlink-ptx)
[2026-03-10T15:02:01Z] shard1 -> selected kernel: matmul_generic_fp16 (fallback: PCIe-serial)
```

alejandra: exactly — one side is using the optimized fused attention kernel that assumes low-latency NVLink transfers for KV exchanges; the other side falls back to matmul_generic which doesn't overlap comm/compute as well. that mismatch forces extra all_reduce windows and prevents continuous streaming of KV slots.

ryan: did the profiler show where time is being spent? e.g., compute vs waiting on comm?

maya: flame graph + trace shows long waits on "nvlink_hop_bridge0" and then a big chunk in "all_reduce_wait". small excerpt:
```
0.0s compute_forward (40%)
0.4s nvlink_hop_bridge0 (15%)
1.1s all_reduce_wait (28%)
0.6s kv_prefetch_pcie_copy (12%)
```

ryan: if the topology forces one pair to route via a bridge (nvlink hop + PCIe) then the kernel latency assumptions break. two short ideas: 1) force kernel homogeneity by making kernelselect avoid fused kernels when any replica will route over PCIe, or 2) change batching slice so KV prefetches issue earlier (more overlap).

jon: option 1 is conservative and likely fixes correctness/perf but costs baseline perf on fully-NVLink runs. option 2 is more surgical. can we quantify the tradeoff quickly?

maya: i ran a quick experiment toggling the heuristic. results (same job id + config):
```
policy=prefer_homogeneous_kernels -> tokens/sec = 3050 (stable across topo)
policy=earlier_kv_prefetch(slice=64->32) -> tokens/sec = 3800 (less variance, slightly higher p99)
```

alejandra: nice. also noticed in the logs that when the fused kernel isn't available it falls back but still expects continuous KV stream sizes; the runtime doesn't adjust its batching window, so you get queuing + larger all-reduce. we should add a small check in kernelselect: if any planned routing path has hop_cost > Xms, downgrade to the conservative kernel or reduce max_slice.

infra-bot: perf-test 2165432100-01 completed: bench-8gpu-mixed-topo. tagged artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/2165432100-01.tar.gz

ryan: actionable plan:
- add a topo probe microbenchmark that returns per-pair hop_cost estimates (maya) :point_right: maya
- implement a kernelselect quick check to prefer homogeneous kernel set when any hop_cost > 1.5ms (alejandra)
- expose a runtime flag `topo_aware_batching=true` to experiment with earlier KV prefetch thresholds (jon/ryan)

maya: i'll start the microbenchmark today. quick prototype command I ran to probe NVLink hop latencies:
```
./comm_probe --pair 0-1 --mode nvlink-hop --iter 1000 --output csv
# sample output: pair,mean_us,median_us,95p_us
0-1,1200,1188,1400
0-2,9400,9360,12000 # routed over PCIe
```

alejandra: for the kernel change, i'll add a unit test that simulates mismatched kernel selection and asserts that the runtime either picks homogeneous kernels or reduces slice to keep in-flight KV size small.

jon: can we also record a perf-flag in the trace when a fallback kernel is chosen? that'll make regression hunting easier.

alejandra: yep adding a `kernelselect_reason` tag in the trace events.

maya: sweet. i'll push the microbenchmark results and attach the perf tarball to the ticket #INF-789. next sync tomorrow to see early numbers. :thumbsup:

ryan: thanks — this explains the weird regression we saw on staging yesterday. good call catching it. :white_check_mark:
